title: Expose 'googlesheets4_quiet' in the function API, or advertise it better
description:
I was trying to figure out how to quiet the sheets output messages:

```
✔ Reading from ${BOOK_TITLE}.

✔ Range ''${SHEET_TITLE}''.
```

Naturally, I checked `?read_sheet` to figure this out, expecting a `quiet=` option.

I found none, and might have concluded it's not possible to do so, but I doggedly chased down the source code, clicking through 3 definitions before finding it's possible:

https://github.com/tidyverse/googlesheets4/blob/55cd9fdbf9c74c20de1eeb9ec2629a7d16c76aa4/R/range_speedread.R#L94-L100
https://github.com/tidyverse/googlesheets4/blob/55cd9fdbf9c74c20de1eeb9ec2629a7d16c76aa4/R/utils-ui.R#L131-L140
https://github.com/tidyverse/googlesheets4/blob/55cd9fdbf9c74c20de1eeb9ec2629a7d16c76aa4/R/utils-ui.R#L80-L82

It would be nice to have this directly as an option; otherwise, one of the `@examples` could set this option to demonstrate it.

title: Feature Request: Add Concurrency Handling to sheet_append()
description: I have observed that the `sheet_append()` function does not handle concurrent writes correctly, which can result in issues where concurrent writes overwrite each other's rows. The Google Sheets API v4 already offers method `spreadsheets.values.append` ([ref](https://developers.google.com/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/append)) with parameter `insertDataOption="INSERT_ROWS"` to manage concurrent writes effectively (also see [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39899528/concurrent-rows-appending-in-google-sheets-api-v4)).  Since this functionality does not appear to be available in the `googlesheets4` package, I would like to formally request the addition of this feature.

title: Bug: Use of Null values does not accurately "skip" cells within range_write()
description:
I believe that the results of #203 may have removed the intended functionality from the Googlesheets API - as it now seems there is no way to skip columns or cells when writing data with functions such as `range_write()`. 

My understanding of the Sheets API and specific functions comes from the following pages:
- [Method: spreadsheets.values.batchUpdate - used in range_write()](https://developers.google.com/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/batchUpdate)
- [ValueRange - underlying component that alters data](https://developers.google.com/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values#resource:-valuerange) - I reference this section, as it notes that "For input, supported value types are: bool, string, and double. **Null values will be skipped**. To set a cell to an **empty value, set the string value to an empty string**."

With this, I expect that when using `range_write()` I would be able to use `NA` to specifically write empty values, while using `NULL` to specifically skip editing values. 

I provided the below `reprex`, in which I create a tibble & sheet with a formula column in between, and attempt to edit them, with the goal of essentially "skipping" an edit to the "formula" column, ideally with the use of `NULL` values.

Let me know if you have any questions or if I'm thinking about this wrong - appreciate all the help! 

```r
library(googlesheets4)
library(googledrive)

# Create a general example of a spreadsheet with 3 columns of data, one that is a formula
tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  numeric = 1:100, 
  formula = googlesheets4::gs4_formula("=A2*2"),
  string = c(rep("example 1", 100))
)

# Create the example sheet
ss <- gs4_create(sheets = tbl)

# View the example sheet
gs4_browse(ss)

# The following examples depict attempts to try and edit a sheet while skipping a column with formulas (arrayformulas or formulas)

# ATTEMPT 1: Using NA - this understandably results in the formula column being overwritten with NA values

tbl_2 <- tibble::tibble(
  numeric = 1:100, 
  formula = NA,
  string = c(rep("example 2", 100))
)

edit_sheet_na <- googlesheets4::range_write(ss, data = tbl_2)

# Restore the original data
googlesheets4::range_write(ss, data = tbl)

# ATTEMPT 2: Using Null - this still results in the formula column being overwritten with NA values
# However, I would not expect this behavior based on the Google Documentation referenced in the issue
tbl_3 <- tibble::tibble(
  numeric = 1:100, 
  formula = list(rep(NULL, 100)),
  string = c(rep("example 3", 100))
)

edit_sheet_null <- googlesheets4::range_write(ss, data = tbl_2)

# Restore the original data
googlesheets4::range_write(ss, data = tbl)

googledrive::drive_rm(ss)
```

title: `sheet_append` should allow adding additional columns
description:
`sheet_append` currently is overly strict when appending new rows to an existing sheet, i.e. the appended data must not have more column than the existing sheet. Which makes the whole adding of new rows cumbersome, because what someone currently needs to do is:
- create a subset of the new columns,
- upload this subset with `range_write`,
- append the new row.

The solution (if supported by the Google API) would be maybe an optional parameter `strict = TRUE/FALSE`, indicating what should happen when the new row has more columns than the existing sheet (E.g. error as of now or add the column).

If adding additional columns is not supported by the Google API, then it would be preferable if `sheet_append` could do the above mentioned workaround under the hood.

Note: it is not an option in this use case to simply re-write/overwrite the entire sheet, because it might contain content online that is not part of the sheet that is upload (e.g. a user might have added a comment or applied some formats).

description:
An Excel workbook stored on a google drive looks and feels like a google sheet, but it does not support the API.  The problem is that when trying to connect to the document, the error message is very unhelpful.

```{r}
gs4_deauth()
read_sheet("1qsPaQqiMKLuU3Ksr9NmkKQ8rR_Nmc6jb")
```
This yields the following error:
```
Error in `gargle_abort_request_failed()`:
! Client error: (400) FAILED_PRECONDITION
• Request can not be executed in the current system state, such as deleting a
  non-empty directory.
• This operation is not supported for this document
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
```

It looks like an authentication problem, but it is fact a problem that the Google Sheets API does not support converted Excel Sheets.  The work around is to convert the Excel sheet to a Google Sheet using the "Save as Google Sheet" menu item in the web interface.

Here is the same sheet after saving.
```{r}
gs4_deauth()
read_sheet("1-M_4DQSMTd_xAi8sPcocMVAikUzh7fvi3MDQDCqu70E")
```
This works as expected.

I'm not sure that this is a bug, as there is probably nothing that can be done in the R code that can fix it.  It might be possible to get a better error message though.  

On the other hand, posting this here might be of help to somebody having the same problem.

title: Explicit NULL cells disappear when writing
description:
Recently I have been trying to write some results to existing Google Sheet files and have found two quirks. I think probably by design but I thought I'd raise them as potential features / options to existing functions that can make life a bit easier for the user.

First: writing NULL columns as empty columns, not skipping them.

Let's say I have a tibble of list-columns something like:

```r
tmp <- tibble(A = list(NULL, NULL, NULL), B = list(1, 2, 3))
tmp
# A tibble: 3 x 2
  A      B        
  <list> <list>   
1 <NULL> <dbl [1]>
2 <NULL> <dbl [1]>
3 <NULL> <dbl [1]>
```

When I write this to a sheet using (as far as I can tell) any of the writing functions, the NULL column just gets skipped rather than a blank column being written. This can mean columns get written in the wrong place - e.g. in the above example column B would be written in column A of the Google Sheet because column A would be ignored rather than a blank column being written. Yet a 3 x 2 sheet will result - just with the B column in the A position and a blank column at the end. If that makes sense?! So it's like `write_sheet` knows about the NULL column and makes space for it, but then doesn't actually write it.

Often I am reading in data with some empty columns (which get read in as a NULL column), doing some wrangling, and then writing to a new and/or existing sheet. It would be nice if the "round-trip" was symmetrical in the sense that empty columns get read in as NULL and NULL columns get written as empty columns. Currently I have to force coercion to character when reading with `col_types = 'c'` and then use `mutate(across(everything(), as.list))` to coerce everything back into list columns - then the NULL columns become character columns of NA, which get written as blank values as intended.

title: Design question: other types of sheets API requests and access to CellData manipulation
description:
I am finding myself in a need of accessing the lower-level sheets API functions. Core functionalities of `googlesheets4` are based on operation of tabular `data.frame` data. I guess it is a design choice?

I find myself more in need of cell manipulation and range data access.

Basically, the functionalities I need are regarding:
- manipulation `CellData` eg. styling cells
- creation of merged cells (`mergeCells` request)
- creation of googlesheets charts (`addChart` request)

I've sucessfully created wrappers around these functionalities, and I am now pondering: is there a plan to incorporate these kinds of operations in `googlesheets4` (I would be happy to join up on these with PRs!), or should I develop another package? As I am finding these kind of functionaties hard to incorporate into *tabular* and *dplyr*-y design.

To show what I mean: to create the chart it would be required to access `CellRange` level and develop few more structs to keep it all clean:

```r
# create cell ranges to point to a data
datesRange <- CellRange(
  sheetId = 0,

description:
Hi Jenny!! 

Wanted to raise a potential feature request (if it's not already something in the works/something that may be possible): 

Using the tab/worksheet id as a third way to identify which sheet a user may want to pull data from. 

The [current docs ](https://googlesheets4.tidyverse.org/reference/read_sheet.html) for read_sheet() function state a user can either use the Sheet Name or the Tab Index number to identify the sheet to read. 

An example of what i'm thinking: 

```r
library(googlesheets4)

#using gapminder url:

The worksheet id might be more stable, correct? I haven't seen that change even when changing tab names or tab position. I tried doing some searching through the issues on googlesheets4, did some googling, stackoverflow, but most of my searches bring me to the sheet id, not the worksheet id.

title: Allow sheet_append to match existing sheet format (or add append option to range_write)
description:
When I use `sheet_append` to add rows to an existing sheet, the new rows are all format free - even if the table in the existing sheet contains formatting. It would be nice to have a `reformat = FALSE` option for `sheet_append` similar to `range_write`.

I think the lack of this option is by design - I assume `sheet_append` is literally adding new rows to the sheet as opposed to writing over existing rows - hence they contain no formatting. But, often I am writing to an existing file with formatting and it would be nice if I could use `sheet_append` without having the blank formatting (or add an `append` option to `range_write`, if that's easier). Currently I just use `range_write` with the `reformat = FALSE` option but then I need to do a bit of extra faff to get the starting row from the existing file by reading it in and then using `nrow` - but the file is often very big and takes ages to read in to do that. If it's not too much hassle to fudge a background solution to one of those functions, it would be great.

title: Service Account Token works in RStudio but not when running via Terminal
description:
Hi there, 

First off, just want to thank you for all of your efforts on this package, i use it quite a bit and it is a priceless resource for the teams I support. 

I'm not sure if i've found a bug or it's possible I didn't authorize correctly. I have a workflow in-which I read in a google sheet from one team i support (updates are made daily to it), perform various data cleaning, etc..., split the sheet out by an individual's name, and write those back to a separate google drive folder for another team to utilize. Finally, if a given set of circumstances/changes are made the script sends an email via the gmailr package to certain users (i'm using as many google packages as i can in this one haha). Ultimately, I wanted to schedule this via CRON so I don't have to manually fire the script several times a day. 

I have a service account token set up via my org's cloud platform and have the token in my project (i know this might not be the best place to keep it). 

After i load in my libraries, the first few lines are as follows: 

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(googlesheets4)
library(googledrive)
library(gmailr)

drive_auth(path = here("service_account_token_key.json"))
gs4_auth(path = here("service_account_token_key.json")) #note: i didn't think i needed to auth the gs4 after drive, but i was getting an issue if i didn't have this auth in here
gm_auth_configure(path = here("gmail_auth_sat_key.json"))
gm_auth(email = "myemail", cache = ".secret")

#rest of script reading in data, etcc....
```
The above works totally fine if i'm doing things manually or sourcing the script within RStudio. And when i look at the google drive folder or the google sheet i see that the service account email is making edits (not my personal account email). And the service account email has access/auth to my drive folder and the sheets it pulls from. 

When i go to run the script through my terminal window or via CRON though, i receive the following error:

```r
> Using an auto-discovered, cached token
  To suppress this message, modify your code or options to clearly consent to
  the use of a cached token
  See gargle's "Non-interactive auth" vignette for more details:
  <https://gargle.r-lib.org/articles/non-interactive-auth.html>
> The googledrive package is using a cached token for 'myemail@email.com'
Error: lexical error: invalid char in json text.
                                      /Users/me/client_secret
                     (right here) ------^
Execution halted
```
Wouldn't the drive_auth/gs4_auth pull from the directory it's located in regardless if it's run though terminal/CRON or RStudio? 

My GoogleSheets4 package is 0.3.0.9
Drive is 1.9.0.9
Gargle is 1.1.0

title: xdg-utils is required to open the authentication link
description:
I am not sure if this is inherited from Gargle and I could not find the code responsible for this behavior.
On a system without xdg-utils (minimal container or OS), R will still try to open the link with xdg-open.

The easiest to repro this would be with Rocker's containers.
First obtain a new session with: `docker run -it --rm rocker/tidyverse`
In R:
```r
install.packages("googlesheets4")  
library(googlesheets4)
gs4_auth()
```
returns:

```
Waiting for authentication in browser...
Press Esc/Ctrl + C to abort
sh: 1: xdg-open: not found
```

Ideally, a link would be printed in terminal to copy in a browser manually if xdg-open is not found in $PATH and/or would try using $BROWSER if it exists.

title: Change package lifecycle status to stable
Running into quota issues
description:
We are currently using google sheets for a [research project on crowd forecasts for Covid-19 case and death numbers](https://cmmid-lshtm.shinyapps.io/crowd-forecast/). We are often running into quota limit issues - even though the number of users we have should be well below what Google allows. 

I'm cross-posting this from [stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66186332/googlesheets-quota-limit-issues-possible-failure-to-use-api-key) - please feel free to close this issue if you feel it doesn't belong here. 

I attempted to create a somewhat reproducible example by setting up a new google account and creating a sheet from which to read.

The first thing I tried (without making any changes to the google account) is this:

```r
library(googledrive)
library(googlesheets4)

# Google sheets authentification -----------------------------------------------
options(gargle_oauth_cache = ".secrets")
drive_auth(cache = ".secrets", email = "iamatestotest@gmail.com")
gs4_auth(token = drive_token())

sheet_id <- "1Z2O5Mce_haceWfduLenJQP-hddXF9biY_4Ydob_psyQ"

n_tries <- 50

for (i in 1:n_tries) {
  data <- read_sheet(ss = sheet_id)
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
  print(i)
}
```

From what I understand I should be able to make around 300 read requests per minute, but I'm usually not be able to get the loop to run beyond 30-34. I then also tried to change the settings on https://console.cloud.google.com, but that was also unsuccessful. 

I suspect it might also be an issue with us not using the google API correctly, but I'm unsure whether this bevavior is expected or something odd is going on. 

Thank you very much!

title: Don't know how to coerce an object of class 'sheets_meta/list' into a 'sheets_id'
description:
I have been trying to use the `googlesheets4` using sheetid like below

```r
ss <- googlesheets4::sheets_get(id = xxxyyyzzz)
googlesheets4::read_sheet(ss, sheet = 1)
```
This returns the error
```r
Error: Don't know how to coerce an object of class 'sheets_meta/list' into a 'sheets_id'
```

The tested version was from `CRAN 0.1.0`
However the same code above runs fine on the development version in `Github 0.1.0.9000`
On further investigation I found that the class of `ss` above is `"sheets_meta" "list"`  in the CRAN version however in the GitHub version it is `"sheets_Spreadsheet" "list"`.
This is causing an error inside the `get_cells` function in the line `ssid <- as_sheets_id(ss)`
Could you please let me know when would the develop version be put in the `CRAN` with this fix.

EDIT - I've since found a better solution, as per the Gargle documentation [here](https://gargle.r-lib.org/articles/non-interactive-auth.html#provide-a-service-account-token-directly). See also my post further [down](https://github.com/tidyverse/googlesheets4/issues/189#issuecomment-747328693).

I've been running into a lot of quota limits and since I'm a newbie to both R and Google API / authorisation, I thought I'd post my workaround in case 1) it's useful to others or 2) there is a better solution.

I notice there is a solution posted here - https://github.com/tidyverse/googlesheets4/issues/139 - but I don't understand any of it.

I do have an API key that I can see at https://console.developers.google.com/ and perhaps adding that to my code would improve my quota?

I'm using this to open a browser window to get a token, so maybe I just need to add the api key to this code?

```
if (interactive()){
gs4_auth(
  email = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  scopes = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets",
  # Get cached secret once - comment out for repeated use locally
  #cache = ".secrets",
  # Use once we have the secret cached
  cache = FALSE,
  use_oob = FALSE,
  token = NULL)
}
```

Maybe I just need to add this line?

`gs4_auth_configure(api_key = "MY_API_KEY")`

Anyway, here is my (no doubt ugly) solution to the issue of occassionally hitting quota limits:

```
Speed_Read <- function(l, ...){
  # Set initial sleep and values
  sleep <- 1
  value <- NULL
  while(is.null(value)){
    try(
      value <- lapply(l, function(x){
        range_read(x, ...)
      })
    )
    Sys.sleep(sleep)
    sleep <- sleep + 1
  }
  return(value)
}
```

Essentially, "Speed_Read()" replaces "range_read()" in the rest of my code and it will continually retry the range_read if there is an error, each time adding a little extra delay until the read is successful.

Hope this is useful to someone or there is some feedback on how to improve this function.

```r
protected_ranges <- map(sheets, "protectedRanges")
protected_ranges <- purrr::flatten(protected_ranges)
protected_ranges <- map(protected_ranges, ~ new("ProtectedRange", !!!.x))
protected_ranges <- map(protected_ranges, as_tibble)

```
Once I added an unnecessary protected range in the actual google sheet as a temporary workaround, I didn't have any issues anymore.

title: Ability to change cell formats inside an existing googlesheet
description:
Now that googlesheets4 has achieved stability, we can shift some really serious excel (writing) work from `openxlsx` to `googlesheets4`. The only reason I still use `openxlsx`, even for working within goooglesheets, is that it allows creation of styles (`openxlsx::createStyle`) and conditional formatting (`openxlsx::conditionalFormatting`). The openxlsx workbook formats interwork almost fine while editing as a google sheet once uploaded, although not perfect. A lot of improvement can be brought in and a direct update of gs formats (using googlesheets4 APIs) will be much better than making changes in an offline workbook and uploading it every time.

My order of preference within createStyle function would be (in case the feature needs to be broken up):

1. fontSize
2. wrapText
3. numFmt
4. locked
5. valign
6. halign
7. textdecoration (bold, itallic)
8. bgFill (Background Fill)

Note, I have used `openxlsx::createStyle()` function arguments as a vocabulary only, although we could improve on their structure a bit. Also there are confusing & quirky parameters in `openxlsx` e.g. fgFill fills up colour in a cell rather than bgFill and gridExpand =TRUE is needed almost always while the default is FALSE.

In addition a `setcolwidth` functionality (as in `openxlsx`) is essential, as the existing `range_autofit` does not serve the purpose when a column has lot of text and it needs to be in `wraptext` mode.

Apologies if I used too many `openxlsx` terms but that's the only reference available to move from an excel world to the googlesheets world in R.

Thanks

Sanjay

title: Prevent character cells containing number from being written with an ` appended
description:
Let's say I have to, through no fault of my own (!), write a very non-tidy tibble to a google sheet. One that contains character columns with both actual strings in some cells and only numbers in others.

So, something like:

    library(tidyverse)
    library(googlesheets4)
    df <- tibble(column = c("A", "B", "2", "3.1"))
    write_sheet(df)

Obviously, strictly speaking, these are all characters, but pretend only the A and B "cells" are, and bear with me.

Currently, unless there's an option I've missed, the cells containing numbers will be written with an \` appended in front of the number (e.g. \`3.1), while those with strings won't (e.g. just B). It would be nice if the numbers could be written without the \` too - to save me having to manually go into the sheet afterwards and convert all the number cells to number format.

Edit:

Just for anyone who might encounter a similar issue, assuming there isn't a simple solution to this, I have just thought up a couple of hacky solutions.

1. If the row position of the character and numeric values are constant, then you can use `slice` from dplyr to separate out your tibble into blocks of all character or all numeric sections, do a `type_convert()` from readr on each section, and then use `range_write` to write to the appropriate section of the google sheet.
2. If the row position of the character and numeric values varies, so you cant set up constant sections with `slice`, you can do the same as (1) but slice the tibble row by row, then `type_convert()` and then write using `sheet_append`.

Obviously, these solutions, particularly the second, are a little slow.

description:
Please add the `col_types = cols()` specification, for consistency with {readr}'s [column specification](https://readr.tidyverse.org/reference/cols.html)

Using the example from {googlesheets4} example:

```r
#read_sheet("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1U6Cf_qEOhiR9AZqTqS3mbMF3zt2db48ZP5v3rkrAEJY/edit#gid=780868077")

# the plain `read_sheet()`
read_sheet(gapminder_sheet)

```

Example: read_sheet with "year" column specified as integer.

We can use the current {googlesheets4} syntax (see ["Column specification"](https://googlesheets4.tidyverse.org/reference/range_read.html#column-specification)

```r
read_sheet(gapminder_sheet, col_types = "??i???")
```

But for files with many variables, this syntax can be cumbersome and error-prone (particularly if there are a limited number of variables that need specifying).

Adding `col_types = cols()` functionality would solve this challenge, and be consistent with {readr}.

The syntax would thus look like this:

```r
# set "year" as integer
read_sheet(gapminder_sheet, 
           col_types = cols(
             year = col_integer()
             )
           )
```

Currently, this syntax returns "Error: `col_types` must be character: * `col_types` has class 'col_spec'" -- it took me a while to realize that it's an error because {googlesheets4} doesn't recognize the syntax.

Thanks!

title: Interface questions re: sheets_create() and sheets_write()
description:
`sheets_create()` and `sheets_write()` (which will be aliased to `write_sheet()`) are the first 2 writing functions to roll out (still very alpha).

ATM `sheets_create()`'s signature is like so:

```
sheets_create <- function(name, ..., sheets = NULL) {...}
```

Some usage might look like so:

``` r
(ss <- sheets_create("foofy-foofy", sheets = list(iris = iris, mtcars = mtcars)))
#>   Spreadsheet name: foofy-foofy
#>                 ID: 1xUf42Net8e8oZ_SLaTB6eEsNGr61T4m7eR-B9o0HwRU
#>             Locale: en_US
#>          Time zone: Etc/GMT
#>        # of sheets: 2
#> 
#> (Sheet name): (Nominal extent in rows x columns)
#>         iris: 151 x 5
#>       mtcars: 33 x 11
```

`sheets_create()` creates an entirely new (spread)Sheet and, optionally, populates one or more (work)sheets with data, provided as a named list of data frames via `sheets`. Again, this whole interface is very much in flux.

`sheets_write()` looks like this right now:

``` r
sheets_write <- function(data, ss, sheet = NULL, skip = 0, na = "") {...}
```

where `data` is a data frame, `ss` must be an existing (spread)Sheet, and `sheet` must refer to an existing (work)sheet by name or position.

Some usage looks like:

``` r
> (ss <- sheets_write(ChickWeight, ss = ss, sheet = "whatever"))
Writing to 'finally-writing'
Writing to sheet "whatever"
  Spreadsheet name: finally-writing
                ID: 1Yy77dNjJWPvJFx7ENAQOPhotQMNaZ-5MAL2UDed9i1c
            Locale: en_US
         Time zone: Etc/GMT
       # of sheets: 2

(Sheet name): (Nominal extent in rows x columns)
        iris: 5 x 3
    whatever: 579 x 4
```

**What is the primary argument of `sheets_create()`?**
Is it the `name` of the new (spread)Sheet? *current reality*
Or should it be the data (the data frame or named list of data frames)?

Elsewhere, @Hadley indicated he thinks the primary input of `sheets_create()` should be the data. Possibly because I alluded to `writexl::write_xlsx()`, `openxlsx::write.xlsx()` and all the `write.*()` and `readr::write_*()` functions. But maybe `sheets_write()` is the function to compare to those?

Quandary:

title: Finalize class naming scheme
description:
Currently there are ~3 types of S3 classes in this package. I want to review / affirm the class naming scheme for two types of classes:

  1. User-facing
  1. Derived from the the API spec

The remaining classes are internal and are working fine / names are fine. This includes all the cell and col types (e.g. `CELL_BLANK`, `CELL_NUMERIC`, `COL_LIST`) and `range_spec`.

### User-facing classes:

  * `sheets_id` holds the file ID of a Sheet. It's a string with classes `sheets_id` and `drive_id`, so it will work as the file identifier in a whole host of googlesheets4 and googledrive functions.
  * `sheets_Spreadsheet` holds metadata on a Sheet, including the file ID but also info about the (work)sheets and named ranges inside it. It is a heavily wrangled version of the [`Spreadsheet` schema](https://developers.google.com/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets#Spreadsheet).

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/rrr/googlesheets4")  
#> Loading googlesheets4

sheets_example("deaths")
#> [1] "1tuYKzSbLukDLe5ymf_ZKdQA8SfOyeMM7rmf6D6NJpxg"
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "sheets_id" "drive_id"

x <- sheets_example("deaths") %>% sheets_get()
class(x)
#> [1] "sheets_Spreadsheet" "list"
x
#>   Spreadsheet name: deaths
#>                 ID: 1tuYKzSbLukDLe5ymf_ZKdQA8SfOyeMM7rmf6D6NJpxg
#>             Locale: en
#>          Time zone: America/Los_Angeles
#>        # of sheets: 2
#> 
#> (Sheet name): (Nominal extent in rows x columns)
#>         arts: 1000 x 26
#>        other: 1000 x 26
#> 
#> (Named range): (A1 range)    
#>     arts_data: 'arts'!A5:F15 
#>    other_data: 'other'!A5:F15
str1(x)
#> List of 7
#>  $ spreadsheet_id : chr "1tuYKzSbLukDLe5ymf_ZKdQA8SfOyeMM7rmf6D6NJpxg"
#>  $ spreadsheet_url: chr "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1tuYKzSbLukDLe5ymf_ZKdQA8SfOyeMM7rmf6D6NJpxg/edit"
#>  $ name           : chr "deaths"
#>  $ locale         : chr "en"
#>  $ time_zone      : chr "America/Los_Angeles"
#>  $ sheets         :Classes 'tbl_df', 'tbl' and 'data.frame': 2 obs. of  8 variables:
#>  $ named_ranges   :Classes 'tbl_df', 'tbl' and 'data.frame': 2 obs. of  10 variables:
#>  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "sheets_Spreadsheet" "list"
```

<sup>Created on 2019-11-30 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0.9001)</sup>

I'm not sure I like the `sheets_Spreadsheet` class name, i.e. the mixed casing and perhaps `Spreadsheet` itself (although it is connected to the `Spreadsheet` schema). It's conceivable that other schemas could get similar treatment later, so we have to think about how this pattern scales.

### Sheets v4 schemas

There are ~200 of these and I need to be able to create and parse many of them (though no where near all 200). These are internal classes.

  * `data-raw/discovery-doc-prep.R` causes selected schemas to be rectangled and stored in the internal `.tidy_schemas` object. When a schema becomes relevant to me, I add it here.
  * The functions in [schemas.R](https://github.com/tidyverse/googlesheets4/blob/master/R/schemas.R) make it easy to instantiate these classes, with some light validation, via generics `new()` and `patch()`.
  * Instances of these types have a class vector identifying the specific schema, declaring that it is a schema, and `list` (to make `jsonlite::toJSON()` happy).

``` r
devtools::load_all("~/rrr/googlesheets4")
#> Loading googlesheets4
class(new("Spreadsheet"))
#> [1] "googlesheets4_Spreadsheet" "googlesheets4_schema"     
#> [3] "list"
class(new("Sheet"))
#> [1] "googlesheets4_Sheet"  "googlesheets4_schema" "list"
class(new("GridRange"))
#> [1] "googlesheets4_GridRange" "googlesheets4_schema"   
#> [3] "list"
```

<sup>Created on 2019-11-30 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0.9001)</sup>

Things to think about: confirm I want to use `sheets_*` for the user-facing classes and `googlesheets4_*` for internal schema-based classes. The relationship between a schema's user facing class (e.g. `sheets_Spreadsheet`) and its internal class (`googlesheets4_Spreadsheet`).

title: [FR] sheets_clear() and sheets_write()
description:
Hi Jenny, here's my feature request for version-1 `sheets_clear() ` and `sheets_write()` functions.

# sheets_clear()
```
sheets_clear <- function(ss, sheet = NULL, range = NULL){
  ### How it works:
  # This method clears the contents of a range
  # 'ss' must identify an existing google sheet
  # 'sheet' identifies a worksheet, just as in sheets_read()
  # 'range' (optional) identifies a range of cells to be cleared, just as in sheets_read(). 
  #  If not given, the whole worksheet will be cleared.
  
  # ...
}
```

# sheets_write()
```
sheets_write <- function(ss = NULL, df, sheet = NULL, top_left_row = 1, top_left_col = 1, top_left_range = NULL, 
                         row_names = FALSE, col_names = TRUE, with_filter = TRUE){
  
  ### How it works:
  # This method does one of two things. If 'ss' is NULL, it creates a new google sheet and adds data to it.
  # Otherwise, it overwrites/adds the data to an existing google sheet.
  # 'df' should be a data.frame we want to slap onto some google sheet
  # 'sheet' identifies a worksheet, just as in sheets_read()
  # The location of the data we're putting on the sheet is given by either
  #  1. a combination of 'top_left_row' and 'top_left_col' or
  #  2. 'top_left_range'. (The top left cell of the given range will be used. If the range contains > 1 cell, 
  #     warn the user)
  # 'row_names' and 'col_names' determine whether to include row and col names
  # 'with_filter' determines whether to apply row filters to the top row of the newly added data
  
}
```

# Notes
- [openxlsx::writeData()](https://github.com/awalker89/openxlsx/blob/master/R/writeData.R) writes data to an excel worksheet, and it's fairly good at its job. It's worth reviewing.
- My `sheets_write()` function can only write one dataframe at a time. I had an obvious desire to generalize this into a named list that could write multiple dataframes, but I **strongly** suggest avoiding this complexity (for now) and focus on writing one dataframe to a sheet.
- I'm assuming NAs will be written as empty strings or however Google Sheets treats missing data
- Not sure the best way to handle Inf and -Inf. Perhaps use the largest value Google Sheets supports
- I haven't even tried to figure out an interface for applying formats. This is important, but I still see it as a v2 kind of thing. 
- Adding hyperlinks to text is something I do a lot, but I also see it as a v2 item.
- I don't mess with named ranges much, but I'm sure some people do. Updating a named range might require different functionality, and may be better suited for a separate function
- `sheets_clear()` is important because, suppose you have a worksheet with a table of 10 rows and you want to update it in a way that reduces it to 8 rows. `sheets_write()` by itself cannot do that. You need to make successive calls, `sheets_clear()` >> `sheets_write()`. Maybe some won't like it, but I think this design is fine (Separation of Concerns, Modularity, ... and all that)

Cheers

ss %>%

title: Googlesheets4 now requires OAuth credentials to read a public Google sheet
description:
The following reprex attempts to read the publicly readable sheet [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1h7SsH6S2ZdPYJuYFxMn6YRUZGbPD1EloZwyuWgBr1hs](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1h7SsH6S2ZdPYJuYFxMn6YRUZGbPD1EloZwyuWgBr1hs).  Unlike older versions of the code, the current one (commit [e0f9eca](https://github.com/tidyverse/googlesheets4/commit/e0f9eca939eb0a756003b03106b108edf1a82b0c)) now asks for OAuth authentication (I think) and asks via a web browser to "Choose an account to continue to tidyverse api packages" (whatever that means - who am I giving authority to?).  This seems unnecessary for reading a public sheet, and makes running scripts offline require storing OAuth tokens and so forth.

It would be good if authentication were only required for reading/writing non-public sheets (or more explicitly: for reading non-public sheets or writing non-publicly-writable sheets).  That could presumably be achieved by making the package less "clever", and explicitly requiring the R user to make a call to an appropriate OAuth function before attempting to access such a sheet.

Here is a reprex for the above-mentioned Google sheet; it should obviously be run from a clean R environment without any credentials being stored in ~/.R/gargle/gargle-oauth:

```r
#! /usr/bin/env Rscript

library(googlesheets4)

test_sheet <- read_sheet("1h7SsH6S2ZdPYJuYFxMn6YRUZGbPD1EloZwyuWgBr1hs")

```

Thanks!
